Art direction is "Cinematic Portfolio" — Full-bleed imagery, inspection-led motion, portrait-weighted media. Art Direction Family "bold", pack "bold.cinematic-portfolio": compose creatively inside this grammar and never switch family. depth.rule: Every route must render at least its declared minSections content sections (hero excluded from the floor only when the page declares 4). Never ship a page with two or three blocks. Each page follows its own surfaceRhythm and ctaEmphasis so no two pages of this site read the same, and no page reuses another page's section order.

geometry.rule: Style with these tokens only. Never write px/rem/vh/vw/%/clamp()/calc() literals in Tailwind arbitrary values or inline styles, and never author raw CSS or <style> tags.

artDirection.name: Cinematic Portfolio
artDirection.description: Full-bleed imagery, inspection-led motion, portrait-weighted media.
artDirection.rule: Author every page inside the "Cinematic Portfolio" design system: Full-bleed imagery, inspection-led motion, portrait-weighted media. Typography is "Helvetica Neue" display at weight 500 over ui-sans-serif body; gradient language is "ink-fade" (use ut-gradient-hero / ut-gradient-panel / ut-gradient-text, never a hand-written gradient); spacing density is "gallery" (use ut-grid / ut-stack / ut-block / ut-pad, never literal gap or padding values); the hero is "full-bleed" aligned start (use ut-hero + ut-hero-media, never a different hero composition); badges, tags and eyebrows use ut-pill / ut-eyebrow so the "underline-caps" shape language stays consistent; entrance motion is "slow-pan" via ut-reveal and ut-reveal-2/3/4 for stagger. Use the ut-* primitives and --ut-* tokens for type scale, surfaces, media framing and motion. Do not invent a competing visual language, and never substitute hardcoded sizes, radii, shadows or gradients for these tokens.

chrome.rule: The canonical SiteShell owns route truth: every navbar and footer link is a PageRegistry projection, supplied below as chrome.navigation. The router renders routes only — it never injects a navbar or a footer, and there is no platform-owned chrome module, so each page renders its own header and footer inline (a floating bar, a plain header, a hand-authored <nav>, or the shared <FloatingNavbar brand={...} links={...} ctaLabel={...} /> from "@/unison/ui"). You choose how the chrome LOOKS; you never choose which links it carries — use chrome.navigation.primary verbatim (same labels, same hrefs, same order) for the primary nav and chrome.navigation.footer for the footer route column. Never invent, rename, drop or re-point a route link, never render two competing primary nav bars or two footers on one page, and never emit /src/sections/SiteNavbar.tsx or /src/sections/SiteFooter.tsx.

navigation.rule: Primary navigation (PageRegistry order, exact labels and hrefs): Home → #/ | Studio → #/about | Work → #/work. These links are route truth. Never invent, rename, drop, reorder or re-point them; design freedom applies to the presentation only.
